submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path lane, 2026-08-15. Owner instruction, chat 2026-08-15: "scan level exclusion". Handoff HANDOFF_2026-08-15_continue_here.md section B.
rationale:
The unverified-claims discovery check has never filtered on page status. That was deliberate and documented, and it has one consequence nobody wanted: a page that was drafted, rejected and archived without ever being deployed is still scanned on every daily sweep, still files claim findings, and has no route to closure. The live instance is webdesign.uk/index-rejected-v1-20260806 (page b9c9a2a3, status archived, deployed_at NULL, build_status needs_rebuild), carrying 19 banned-claim findings on review-queue item a355d78b. Those 19 findings are about copy no visitor can reach, and the item has come back on every sweep since the instrument shipped.

The fix is one predicate. What makes it worth a review round is the SHAPE of that predicate, not its size. The obvious spelling is `p.status <> 'archived'`, it is what five other page-selection call sites in this estate use as their liveness test, and it is WRONG HERE — measured, not argued. On 2026-08-15, of the 11 archived pages carrying scannable components, FIVE were serving HTTP 200 to the public. Archiving a page sets a database column; it does not remove the artefact already committed to the deploy repo. So the exclusion must be the CONJUNCTION archived AND never-deployed, which drops exactly the one page that was never published and keeps every page that might still be readable.

I am submitting because this narrows what a SHARED scanner covers, and because it deletes a property that a doc comment states in terms. Both are things a reviewer should get to see rather than discover.

plan.summary: Add one predicate to ScanDeployedClaims' page query — AND NOT (p.status = 'archived' AND p.deployed_at IS NULL) — so archived, never-deployed pages stop being claim-scanned. Rewrite the doc comment that currently states the opposite property, update the revalidator's page_absent reason so an operator can tell an excluded page from a deleted one, and pin the conjunction with a contract test that fails on either half alone. Fleet-wide effect today: 1 page / 7 components leave scope; 11 archived-but-deployed pages (5 of them serving HTTP 200) stay in scope.

edits.rationale: The exclusion itself. Placed on the page query only — site_components rows hang off the site, not a page, so there is no page status to filter there. Both halves are load-bearing: the status half alone would stop claim-checking five live pages (measured), and the deployed_at half alone would drop every active page not yet shipped, which is precisely the pre-publication surface bugs_open/093 added content_data scanning to cover.
edits.sketch:
WHERE p.site_id = $1
+      AND NOT (p.status = 'archived' AND p.deployed_at IS NULL)
       AND ( (pc.rendered_html IS NOT NULL AND pc.rendered_html <> '')
          OR (pc.content_data IS NOT NULL AND pc.content_data::text <> '{}') )

edits.rationale: THIS EDIT DELETES A DOCUMENTED PROPERTY ON PURPOSE, and I am naming it rather than letting a reviewer find it. The block currently opens '⚠ NO PAGE-STATUS FILTER, and that is deliberate' and closes 'Widening or narrowing it here would silently change what the CHECK reports.' That was true and is now false. The replacement records what the predicate is, why the conjunction rather than the obvious simplification, the five measured 200s with byte counts, and that the estate's usual liveness predicate is the wrong tool for an audit query.
edits.sketch:
-// ⚠ NO PAGE-STATUS FILTER, and that is deliberate ...
+// ⚠ ONE PAGE-STATUS EXCLUSION, added 2026-08-15 ... and it is a CONJUNCTION
+// BOTH HALVES ARE LOAD-BEARING, and that is measured rather than argued.
+// ⚠ THE ESTATE'S USUAL LIVENESS PREDICATE IS THEREFORE WRONG FOR THIS QUERY.

edits.rationale: An excluded page returns no scan row, which this branch reads as page_absent. The verdict is right (refuse, never close) but the operator-facing Reason said 'page is absent', which sends a human looking for a deletion that never happened — and this arm cannot close itself, so a human is exactly who has to act on it. Adds the never-deployed cause to the Reason and rewrites the comment, which also asserted the now-false 'this check has never filtered on page status'.
edits.sketch:
-Reason: "page is absent, or has no component carrying rendered html or stored content, ..."
+Reason: "page is absent, archived without ever having been deployed, or has no component carrying rendered html or stored content, ... an unbuilt or never-published page is not evidence the claims were removed"

edits.rationale: Contract test on the SQL the scan actually issues, reusing the sibling lockedskip file's sqlmock harness rather than standing up a second one. Honest about its ceiling: sqlmock does not execute predicates, so this cannot show Postgres selects the right rows — that half was established against the live database and the numbers are recorded in the header. Tests 2 and 3 exist specifically to fail the two weakenings, since the status-alone version is the one that reads as a tidy-up and costs five live pages.
edits.sketch:
const theExclusion = "NOT (p.status = 'archived' AND p.deployed_at IS NULL)"
TestPageQueryExcludesArchivedAndNeverDeployed  // diagnoses WHICH half was lost
TestExclusionIsNotStatusAlone                  // skips (not passes) if test 1 owns the failure
TestExclusionIsNotNeverDeployedAlone
TestSiteChromeQueryCarriesNoPageStatusFilter

edits.rationale: Asserts the shipped Reason still distinguishes its three causes and still says the absence is not evidence the claims were removed. Checks by concept (one word per cause) rather than exact prose, and the header states the resulting ceiling explicitly: it catches a cause being deleted, not a cause being described badly.

got := unverifiedClaimsVerdict("p1", filedAt, flaggedHero, nil, publishedAfterEdit())
// premise check on Arm first, then: "absent" / "never" / "no component" / "not evidence"

grounded_in: The property being deleted, verbatim from check_unverified_claims.go:338 before this change: '⚠ NO PAGE-STATUS FILTER, and that is deliberate — it differs from ScanVoiceTells, which restricts to p.status IN (active,deployed). This check has never filtered on page status, and the revalidator must judge by exactly the predicate the emit side uses or the two ends disagree. Widening or narrowing it here would silently change what the CHECK reports.'

THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-15, curl against production with a fabricated-URL control on each domain returning 404 at a different byte count: fundamentallyai.com/blog/ai-readiness-checker-guide.html 200/25861 (control 404/2697); fundamentallyai.com/tools/llm-cost-calculator/index.html 200/35331 (control 404/2697); leopardessconsulting.co.uk/our-approach.html 200/28948 (control 404/2711); robot-hands.com/gripper-catalog.html 200/30997 (control 404/2886); robot-hands.com/news.html 200/48047 (control 404/2886). All five have pages.status='archived'. Six further archived pages returned 404 byte-identical to their control. An archived page CAN be serving.

Blast radius, live DB 2026-08-15. Pages carrying scannable components: active/deployed 610, active/never-deployed 10, archived/deployed 11, archived/never-deployed 1. The exclusion set is that last cell: exactly 1 page, 7 components — webdesign.uk page b9c9a2a3 'index-rejected-v1-20260806', url /index.html, status archived, build_status needs_rebuild, deployed_at NULL.

The excluded URL stays covered. webdesign.uk has TWO page rows at /index.html: 4f180f39 'index' (active, deployed 2026-08-14 22:07) and b9c9a2a3 'index-rejected-v1-20260806' (the excluded draft). Excluding the draft does not stop /index.html being claim-checked.

Open-item impact, joined on result->'revalidation'->'evidence'->>'page_id': of 19 open claims_unverified items, 16 resolve to a page row; 4 sit on never-deployed pages, 2 on archived pages, and exactly 1 on both — a355d78b. A first attempt at this join keyed on result->'revalidation'->>'page_id' and matched NOTHING, returning a uniform 'never deployed = true' for all 19 rows that looked like a finding; the count(p.id) control is what exposed it.

The contrary precedent, and why it does not apply. LANDMINES.md (2026-08-03, bugs_open/098 lane): 'build_status=deployed is not the platform still wants this page served — a selector keyed on it alone RESURRECTS retired pages ... Archiving sets status and leaves build_status untouched ... the check: pair them — AND p.build_status = 'deployed' AND p.status = 'active' — as load_site_pages_action.go:80, plan_sections_action.go:247, maintenance_actions.go:751, request_render_audit_action.go:110 and store_generated_component_action.go:873 already do.' That is the correct predicate for 'should we RE-PUBLISH this page' and the wrong one for 'is there copy a visitor can read'. Applying it here would have excluded all 12 archived pages including the 5 measured serving.

The sibling scanner's shape, for the parity question. ScanVoiceTells (check_voice_tells.go:176) restricts to p.status IN ('active','deployed'). pages.status takes exactly two values fleet-wide — active 658, archived 36 — so 'deployed' matches nothing there and the voice scan drops every archived page, including the 5 that are serving. This change does NOT harmonise the two; it leaves the claims scan strictly wider. Flagged as a separate question rather than fixed inside a bug patch.

Test evidence is mutation, not a green run. Against a clean `git archive HEAD` tree (another session had check_missing_structure.go dirty in the same package), with an unmutated control first that produced no failures: drop the exclusion -> caught by test 1; weaken to status alone -> tests 1 and 2; weaken to deployed_at alone -> tests 1 and 3; move a page-status filter onto the site query -> tests 1 and 4; full revert of the Reason text -> caught; drop the 'not evidence' clause -> caught. A partial revert that leaves the word 'never' standing elsewhere is NOT caught, and the test header says so.
plan.risks:
1. SHARED SEAM, CONSUMERS NAMED NOT MEASURED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). ScanDeployedClaims has two live consumers and they are the two ends of one item's life: the emit side, UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run (check_unverified_claims.go:86, pageIDFilter "", fleet-wide on the discovery rotation), and the review-queue revalidator (revalidate_unverified_claims.go:199, one page), driven by revalidate_review_queue_action.go. What changes about their guarantee: both previously judged EVERY page with stored content and now judge every such page except archived-and-never-deployed. They change together, which is the point of the sharing — the predicate-parity doc comment from council round 6 exists so the two ends cannot answer the same question differently. There is no third consumer; the only other references are tests.

2. THIS DOES NOT RETIRE a355d78b, AND A READER WILL ASSUME IT DOES. An excluded page returns no scan row, so the revalidator takes the scan == nil branch and returns revalidationUnknown with arm page_absent — a REFUSAL, not a closure. The item stays open, on a different arm, and the fleet page_absent count goes 2 -> 3. Disposing of the item is a separate, explicit act. I have deliberately NOT cancelled it yet: leaving it open means the next daily sweep after this ships will show it move scan_still_trips -> page_absent, which is the only live proof the exclusion fired. Cancelling it first would destroy that evidence.

3. POSSIBLE ARCHITECTURE SCOPE — FLAGGED, NOT DECIDED. The 2026-07-29 ruling makes the test 'does it change what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES?'. This narrows what a shared scanner covers, so the honest answer is arguably yes; against that, it removes no capability and adds no authority, the vocabulary is unchanged, and the affected set is one never-published page. I am not deciding it silently in either direction — if the seats rule this needs an RFC, that is the answer and I will route it.

4. THE HANDOFF THAT SPECIFIED THIS CITED ITS OWN JUSTIFICATION WRONG, and the conclusion survived anyway. HANDOFF_2026-08-15 §B.2 justified the conjunction by citing a LANDMINES.md entry titled 'an archived page can be SERVING'. No entry with that wording exists; the nearest one argues close to the reverse (status is the retirement signal, build_status is the misleading one) and prescribes the predicate that would have been wrong here. I did not inherit the conclusion — the five 200s are a fresh measurement, and they happen to vindicate it. Recording this because a reviewer checking the citation will find it does not say what it was said to say.

5. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX. Six archived-but-deployed pages return 404 and are still scanned, so findings filed against them are still hard to close; that is deliberate conservatism, since 404-now does not prove 404-later while the row says deployed. And the exclusion is invisible until a fleet roll — Go changes are inert until the image is rebuilt, so the 2026-08-16 sweep will run the old binary.
